title: Elapsed Time Word Problems
intro: Distinguish a clock time from an amount of elapsed time.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Mark the start and finish on a timeline. Model useful jumps through the next hour, or work backward when the start is unknown.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

8:45 → 9:00 → 9:12
+15 minutes, then +12 minutes
Elapsed time: 27 minutes

The hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Subtracting the clock digits as ordinary whole numbers would not measure the time correctly.

Ask your student

Are we finding a time on the clock or a number of minutes?

If your student needs help

If the student treats time as base ten, mark the sixty minutes in an hour.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each sheet reuses six original word problems: two ask for elapsed minutes, two for the finishing time, and two for the starting time. Starts are between 8:00 and 9:59 a.m., and durations are 1 through 89 minutes. All events remain in the same morning.
